- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, cap the peak at 1.5x the 14-day moving average to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, favor mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.  
- If true outcome is consistently lower than forecast in early days of the 30d window, apply a 3–5% downward bias to next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), reduce forecast slope by 20–30% to avoid overreacting to short-term noise.
